title: Latency sentinel: p95/p99 slice visualizer and regression alerting by endpoint+model+region
text:
Latency sentinel: p95/p99 slice visualizer and regression alerting by endpoint+model+region

description:
Goal: Build a lightweight "sentinel" layer and visualization that surfaces p95 and p99 latency regressions broken down by route (API endpoint), served model variant, and region. This ticket wires the sentinel into existing synthetic load harnesses and live telemetry rollups, provides an interactive slice visualizer for on-call and SRE use, and plumbs regression alerting to PagerDuty/Slack.

Background: We already collect per-request traces and produce rollups, but teams struggle to quickly answer: 'Which model/route/region caused the p99 spike after the deploy?' Current dashboards aggregate at a route level and lack easy comparison across model variants and regions. This work aims to: reduce mean time to detect (MTTD) by surfacing anomalous percentile shifts, correlate with tokens/sec and synthetic-run results, and offer fast drilldowns.

Scope:
- Implement sentinel job that computes daily and hourly slice-level p95/p99 deltas and baseline percentiles (7d/28d).
- Add an interactive visualizer in Console: multiselect axis of route, model, region, time-window; heatmap for percentile delta; click-to-query raw traces.
- Integrate synthetic load harness runs (tokens/sec) so visualizer can overlay synthetic-run p99 points and indicate whether regressions are reproducible under controlled load.
- Add automated regression detector (statistical + rule-based) with configurable thresholds and automatic suppression for low-cardinality slices.
- Wire alerts (Slack + PagerDuty) with contextual links to the visualizer, failing synthetic-run artifacts, and suggested rollback options.

Non-goals: Full histogram retention of every request (we'll rely on pre-aggregated histogram store), changing global SLO definitions, or reworking token billing metrics.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Pre-aggregated rollups vs raw histogram scans: rollups are cheaper at scale but reduce ability to compute arbitrary quantiles; we will store 1-minute histograms with computed p95/p99 to balance cost and fidelity.
- Cardinality explosion: we limit sentinel to route+model+region slices with optional 'tag' field; sampling rules applied for low-traffic models to avoid noisy alerts.
- Alert sensitivity: default to medium sensitivity with an adaptive window (baseline 7d, but sliding to 28d in low-traffic slices).

acceptance_criteria:
Sentinel batch job producing hourly p95 and p99 per route+model+region into observability DB (schema documented in Confluence)
Console visualizer accessible under Observability > Latency Sentinels with filters for route, model, region, and time window
Heatmap + time-series view supports overlay of synthetic harness p99 points and tokens/sec line
Regression detector generates alert payloads with links to visualizer, top-3 contributing slices, and the latest synthetic-run logs
Unit and integration tests for sentinel logic; e2e test that triggers an intentional regression in staging synthetic harness and validates alert flow

implementation_plan:
1) Sentinel worker: implement histogram aggregation and baseline computation (backend)
2) Regression detector: statistical engine + rule layer; add suppression for low-cardinality
3) Observability API: top-k slices and synthetic overlay endpoints
4) Console UI: heatmap, time-series overlay, drilldown to traces
5) Alerts: templated message + runbook links
6) E2E: synthetic-run replay and alert verification

risks:
Cardinality blowup leading to increased DB storage and query costs; noisy alerts for infrequent slices; mismatch between synthetic harness and production traffic patterns leading to false positives/negatives.

mitigations:
Limit default slice dimensions; apply adaptive sampling; incremental rollout behind feature flag; set conservative default alert thresholds and provide easy tuning UI.

notes:
Next steps: finish sentinel job instrumentation (metrics + tags), land observability API change (ENG-17535), and iterate on visualizer accessibility. Coordinate with product for alert cadence and on-call playbook. Schedule a stakeholder review 2025-10-07.

2025-09-25 - Priya Patel (SRE): Synthetic harness integration validated for tokens/sec overlay; observed one false positive on a low-volume slice — added suppression rules to spec.
2025-09-30 - Marco Ruiz (Design): Uploaded mockups for visualizer (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1VizMockups. Design feedback: make heatmap color scale consistent with Console palettes; add quick-compare for two model variants.
2025-10-02 - Liam O'Connor: Began Console frontend implementation branch. Need API changes in observability service to return top-k contributing slices for a given alert. Filed dependency ticket ENG-17535 for API contract.
